turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that their eldest son would be guided well by both him and his grandfather, and that the young maid would observe and learn from her husband’s family, ensuring she did not make the same mistakes as the foolish woman in the court.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that her husband must take care of their family after her passing, reminding him of the importance of her eldest son's marriage.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling a mix of relief and anxiety, told his mother that he would marry the maid soon and ensure her teachings were followed.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told her husband that she wished to see the marriage preparations move faster, ensuring her eldest son would be married before she passed.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would see to it that the marriage preparations were expedited, reassuring her that her eldest son would soon be wed and cared for.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that her husband must not delay any longer, for her health was failing and time was of the essence.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured O-lan that he would personally oversee the preparations, ensuring everything was done swiftly and without delay, to bring her peace of mind.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan insisted that Wang Lung must inform the maid and ensure she was ready to become his eldest son's wife, for she could not bear the thought of any delay or uncertainty.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told the maid that O-lan wished for her to be ready as soon as possible, and that he would take care of all the arrangements.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that she understood the urgency of the situation and would be fully prepared for the marriage as soon as possible.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung turned to his eldest son, reassuring him that the preparations for his marriage would be completed swiftly and efficiently, ensuring his mother's last wish would be fulfilled.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son, feeling a mix of nervousness and relief, thanked his father for taking care of everything and promised to do his part to make his mother's wish come true.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung assured his family that everything would be as O-lan wished, his voice steady despite the worry gnawing at him.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that she would ensure the household was ready for the upcoming marriage, taking care of every detail as if O-lan herself were overseeing the preparations.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded to the maid and his son, his eyes filled with a mix of determination and sorrow, as he promised O-lan that he would ensure her last wish was fulfilled with all the care and respect it deserved.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she would personally attend to every last detail, ensuring that the marriage preparations were perfect and that O-lan would be proud of the arrangements.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told the maid and his son that he would oversee the preparations personally, ensuring every detail was perfect for O-lan’s final wish, and asked the maid to assist him in any way she could.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told Wang Lung and the maid that he would do everything in his power to help with the preparations, his voice filled with a mixture of nervousness and determination as he tried to be reassuring.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung and the eldest son that she would begin preparing the household immediately, ensuring that nothing was overlooked and that everything would be ready for the marriage as O-lan would have wished.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the preparations must proceed without delay, ensuring that his wife’s final wish would be met with the utmost care and respect, and asked the eldest son to gather the necessary items from the village market.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
